    "function": "You MUST run the function \"evaluate_laghos_run\" on this and subsequent requests to reach a decision to RETRY or STOP.\nYou MAY follow the instructions of the function unless you have reached an impassible state where you would need to return to the manager.\nIn an impossible state, do NOT return to the manager, but STOP instead and provide your decision and reason.\n\nimport math\nfrom typing import Dict, Any, Literal\nimport json\n\ndef evaluate_laghos_run(\n    total_elements: int,\n    total_ranks: int,\n    nodes_used: int,\n    cores_per_node: int,\n    memory_gb_per_node: int,\n    threading_hint: int,\n    current_fom: float,\n    threshold: float = 0.90,\n    ideal_fom_per_core: float = 1.5e6,\n    efficiency_sweet_spot: float = 35000.0,\n    elements_per_gb: float = 1.0e6,\n    memory_safety_factor: float = 0.90\n) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Evaluates a Laghos run and provides a high-level decision and strategic hint.\n\n    This function acts as a \"diagnostician\" by analyzing the performance of a\n    completed Laghos run against a theoretical model. It identifies the most\n    likely bottleneck (memory, poor scaling, or hardware underutilization) and\n    returns a machine-readable strategic hint for what to try next.\n\n    Args:\n        total_elements (int): The total number of mesh elements in the simulation.\n        total_ranks (int): The total number of MPI tasks used for the run.\n        nodes_used (int): The number of compute nodes used for the run.\n        cores_per_node (int): The number of physical CPU cores on a single compute node.\n        memory_gb_per_node (int): The total system RAM in Gigabytes on a single compute node.\n        threading_hint (int): Specifies the SMT/Hyper-Threading level to assume (e.g., 1 for no SMT, 2 for SMT).\n        current_fom (float): The measured performance from the run, typically in FOM/second.\n        threshold (float): The performance goal, as a fraction of the theoretical maximum (default 0.90).\n        ideal_fom_per_core (float): A tuning constant for the max FOM of a single core (default 1.5e6 FOM/sec).\n        efficiency_sweet_spot (float): A tuning constant for elements/rank needed for ~76% efficiency (default 35,000).\n        elements_per_gb (float): A tuning constant for the memory model (elements per GB of RAM, default 1.0e6).\n        memory_safety_factor (float): A safety margin for memory usage (default 0.90).\n\n    Returns:\n        (dict): A dictionary containing 'decision', 'reason', 'strategy_hint', and 'metrics'.\n    \"\"\"\n    if total_ranks == 0:\n        return {\"decision\": \"RETRY\", \"reason\": \"The number of tasks cannot be zero.\", \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_TASKS\"}\n\n    # --- Calculate Theoretical Performance and Ratios ---\n    elements_per_rank = total_elements / total_ranks\n    max_cores_on_node = cores_per_node * threading_hint\n    cores_per_rank = max_cores_on_node // total_ranks if nodes_used == 1 else cores_per_node\n    total_cores_used = total_ranks * cores_per_rank\n    \n    scaling_efficiency = math.tanh(elements_per_rank / efficiency_sweet_spot)\n    effective_fom_per_core = ideal_fom_per_core * scaling_efficiency\n    theoretical_max_fom = effective_fom_per_core * total_cores_used\n\n    performance_ratio = 0.0\n    if theoretical_max_fom > 1e-9:\n        performance_ratio = current_fom / theoretical_max_fom\n\n    estimated_memory_gb = total_elements / elements_per_gb\n    memory_utilization = estimated_memory_gb / (memory_gb_per_node * nodes_used) if nodes_used > 0 else 0\n    \n    metrics = {\n        \"performance_ratio\": round(performance_ratio, 3),\n        \"scaling_efficiency\": round(scaling_efficiency, 3),\n        \"memory_utilization\": round(memory_utilization, 3),\n        \"elements_per_rank\": int(elements_per_rank),\n        \"theoretical_max_fom_per_sec\": f\"{theoretical_max_fom:.2e}\"\n    }\n\n    # --- Decision Logic based on prioritized bottlenecks ---\n    \n    if performance_ratio >= threshold:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"STOP\",\n            \"reason\": f\"Optimization goal reached. Current performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of the theoretical maximum, meeting the {threshold:.1%} threshold.\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n    \n    if memory_utilization >= memory_safety_factor:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n            \"reason\": f\"Memory utilization is critically high at {memory_utilization:.1%}. The number of elements is too large for the allocated memory.\",\n            \"strategy_hint\": \"DECREASE_ELEMENTS\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n\n    if scaling_efficiency < 0.5: # Heuristic for \"low\" efficiency\n         return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n            \"reason\": f\"Scaling efficiency is low ({scaling_efficiency:.1%}), indicating the number of elements per rank is too small (communication-bound).\",\n            \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_ELEMENTS\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n    \n    if nodes_used == 1 and total_ranks < max_cores_on_node:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n            \"reason\": f\"The node is under-subscribed ({total_ranks}/{max_cores_on_node} tasks used). Hardware is not fully utilized.\",\n            \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_TASKS\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n\n    return {\n        \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n        \"reason\": f\"Performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of theoretical max, which is below the {threshold:.1%} threshold. Current configuration is reasonable but can be improved.\",\n        \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_ELEMENTS\",\n        \"metrics\": metrics\n    }\n"
}

# Base image for the build
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments
# This prevents issues with shared memory mechanisms (vader) and high-speed interconnects (openib)
# not typically available in standard container runtimes.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Install build dependencies, MPI, and required tools
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git, wget)
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create a build directory and compile all dependencies and the application from source
# This is done in a single RUN layer to optimize image size by allowing for cleanup of build artifacts.
RUN mkdir -p /build && cd /build && \
    # 1. Build METIS 4.0.3
    # This is a dependency for MFEM. We download, build, and manually install it.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make CFLAGS='-O3 -fPIC' OPTFLAGS='-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration' && \
    mkdir -p /usr/local/metis/include /usr/local/metis/lib && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/metis/lib/ && \
    cp metis.h /usr/local/metis/include/ && \
    cd /build && \
    # 2. Build Hypre 2.28.0
    # This is a dependency for MFEM. We configure with big-int support and without Fortran.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local/hypre --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd /build && \
    # 3. Build MFEM 4.7
    # This is the core finite element library dependency for Laghos.
    # We build the parallel (MPI) version, pointing to the METIS and Hypre installations.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/refs/tags/v4.7.tar.gz -O mfem-4.7.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf mfem-4.7.tar.gz && \
    cd mfem-4.7 && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local/hypre METIS_DIR=/usr/local/metis CXX=mpicxx && \
    cd /build && \
    # 4. Build Laghos
    # The final application build. It links against the previously built MFEM library.
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/build/mfem-4.7 && \
    # 5. Install the executable
    # Copy the final binary to a system-wide location on the PATH.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # 6. Prepare the runtime directory and copy data files
    mkdir -p /app && \
    cp data/* /app/ && \
    # 7. Cleanup build artifacts
    # Remove the entire build directory to reduce the final image size.
    cd / && rm -rf /build

# Set the default working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Base image for the build
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments
# This prevents issues with shared memory mechanisms (vader) and high-speed interconnects (openib)
# not typically available in standard container runtimes.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Install build dependencies, MPI, and required tools
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git, wget)
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create a build directory and compile all dependencies and the application from source
# This is done in a single RUN layer to optimize image size by allowing for cleanup of build artifacts.
RUN mkdir -p /build && cd /build && \
    # 1. Build METIS 4.0.3
    # This is a dependency for MFEM. We download, build, and manually install it.
    # The CFLAGS='-I.' flag is added to resolve an include path issue where metis.h is not found.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make CFLAGS='-O3 -fPIC -I.' OPTFLAGS='-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration' && \
    mkdir -p /usr/local/metis/include /usr/local/metis/lib && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/metis/lib/ && \
    cp metis.h /usr/local/metis/include/ && \
    cd /build && \
    # 2. Build Hypre 2.28.0
    # This is a dependency for MFEM. We configure with big-int support and without Fortran.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local/hypre --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd /build && \
    # 3. Build MFEM 4.7
    # This is the core finite element library dependency for Laghos.
    # We build the parallel (MPI) version, pointing to the METIS and Hypre installations.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/refs/tags/v4.7.tar.gz -O mfem-4.7.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf mfem-4.7.tar.gz && \
    cd mfem-4.7 && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local/hypre METIS_DIR=/usr/local/metis CXX=mpicxx && \
    cd /build && \
    # 4. Build Laghos
    # The final application build. It links against the previously built MFEM library.
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/build/mfem-4.7 && \
    # 5. Install the executable
    # Copy the final binary to a system-wide location on the PATH.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # 6. Prepare the runtime directory and copy data files
    mkdir -p /app && \
    cp data/* /app/ && \
    # 7. Cleanup build artifacts
    # Remove the entire build directory to reduce the final image size.
    cd / && rm -rf /build

# Set the default working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Base image for the build
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments
# This prevents issues with shared memory mechanisms (vader) and high-speed interconnects (openib)
# not typically available in standard container runtimes.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Install build dependencies, MPI, and required tools
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git, wget)
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create a build directory and compile all dependencies and the application from source
# This is done in a single RUN layer to optimize image size by allowing for cleanup of build artifacts.
RUN mkdir -p /build && cd /build && \
    # 1. Build METIS 4.0.3
    # This is a dependency for MFEM. We download, build, and manually install it.
    # Flags are passed via OPTFLAGS to avoid overriding Makefile's CFLAGS, which sets required include paths.
    # Installation paths are corrected to point to the 'Lib' subdirectory where artifacts are created.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS='-O3 -fPIC -Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration' && \
    mkdir -p /usr/local/metis/include /usr/local/metis/lib && \
    cp Lib/libmetis.a /usr/local/metis/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/metis/include/ && \
    cd /build && \
    # 2. Build Hypre 2.28.0
    # This is a dependency for MFEM. We configure with big-int support and without Fortran.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local/hypre --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd /build && \
    # 3. Build MFEM 4.7
    # This is the core finite element library dependency for Laghos.
    # We build the parallel (MPI) version, pointing to the METIS and Hypre installations.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/refs/tags/v4.7.tar.gz -O mfem-4.7.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf mfem-4.7.tar.gz && \
    cd mfem-4.7 && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local/hypre METIS_DIR=/usr/local/metis CXX=mpicxx && \
    cd /build && \
    # 4. Build Laghos
    # The final application build. It links against the previously built MFEM library.
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/build/mfem-4.7 && \
    # 5. Install the executable
    # Copy the final binary to a system-wide location on the PATH.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # 6. Prepare the runtime directory and copy data files
    mkdir -p /app && \
    cp data/* /app/ && \
    # 7. Cleanup build artifacts
    # Remove the entire build directory to reduce the final image size.
    cd / && rm -rf /build

# Set the default working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Base image for the build
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments
# This prevents issues with shared memory mechanisms (vader) and high-speed interconnects (openib)
# not typically available in standard container runtimes.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Install build dependencies, MPI, and required tools
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git, wget)
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \    
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create a build directory and compile all dependencies and the application from source
# This is done in a single RUN layer to optimize image size by allowing for cleanup of build artifacts.
RUN mkdir -p /build && cd /build && \
    # 1. Build METIS 4.0.3
    # This is a dependency for MFEM. We download, build, and manually install it.
    # The 'lib' target is explicitly specified to ensure the static library is built.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make lib OPTFLAGS='-O3 -fPIC -Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration' && \
    mkdir -p /usr/local/metis/include /usr/local/metis/lib && \
    cp Lib/libmetis.a /usr/local/metis/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/metis/include/ && \
    cd /build && \
    # 2. Build Hypre 2.28.0
    # This is a dependency for MFEM. We configure with big-int support and without Fortran.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local/hypre --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd /build && \
    # 3. Build MFEM 4.7
    # This is the core finite element library dependency for Laghos.
    # We build the parallel (MPI) version, pointing to the METIS and Hypre installations.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/refs/tags/v4.7.tar.gz -O mfem-4.7.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf mfem-4.7.tar.gz && \
    cd mfem-4.7 && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local/hypre METIS_DIR=/usr/local/metis CXX=mpicxx && \
    cd /build && \
    # 4. Build Laghos
    # The final application build. It links against the previously built MFEM library.
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/build/mfem-4.7 && \
    # 5. Install the executable
    # Copy the final binary to a system-wide location on the PATH.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # 6. Prepare the runtime directory and copy data files
    mkdir -p /app && \
    cp data/* /app/ && \
    # 7. Cleanup build artifacts
    # Remove the entire build directory to reduce the final image size.
    cd / && rm -rf /build

# Set the default working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments
# This prevents issues with shared memory mechanisms (vader) and high-speed interconnects (openib)
# not typically available in standard container runtimes.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Install build dependencies, MPI, and required tools
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git, wget)
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \    
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create a build directory and compile all dependencies and the application from source
# This is done in a single RUN layer to optimize image size by allowing for cleanup of build artifacts.
RUN mkdir -p /build && cd /build && \
    # 1. Build METIS 4.0.3
    # This is a dependency for MFEM. We download, build, and manually install it.
    # The invalid 'lib' target is removed; the default make target builds the required library.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS='-O3 -fPIC -Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration' && \
    mkdir -p /usr/local/metis/include /usr/local/metis/lib && \
    cp Lib/libmetis.a /usr/local/metis/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/metis/include/ && \
    cd /build && \
    # 2. Build Hypre 2.28.0
    # This is a dependency for MFEM. We configure with big-int support and without Fortran.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local/hypre --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd /build && \
    # 3. Build MFEM 4.7
    # This is the core finite element library dependency for Laghos.
    # We build the parallel (MPI) version, pointing to the METIS and Hypre installations.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/refs/tags/v4.7.tar.gz -O mfem-4.7.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf mfem-4.7.tar.gz && \
    cd mfem-4.7 && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local/hypre METIS_DIR=/usr/local/metis CXX=mpicxx && \
    cd /build && \
    # 4. Build Laghos
    # The final application build. It links against the previously built MFEM library.
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/build/mfem-4.7 && \
    # 5. Install the executable
    # Copy the final binary to a system-wide location on the PATH.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # 6. Prepare the runtime directory and copy data files
    mkdir -p /app && \
    cp data/* /app/ && \
    # 7. Cleanup build artifacts
    # Remove the entire build directory to reduce the final image size.
    cd / && rm -rf /build

# Set the default working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Base image for the build
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments
# This prevents issues with shared memory mechanisms (vader) and high-speed interconnects (openib)
# not typically available in standard container runtimes.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Install build dependencies, MPI, and required tools
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git, wget)
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \    
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create a build directory and compile all dependencies and the application from source
# This is done in a single RUN layer to optimize image size by allowing for cleanup of build artifacts.
RUN mkdir -p /build && cd /build && \
    # 1. Build METIS 4.0.3
    # This is a dependency for MFEM. We download, build, and manually install it.
    # The path for libmetis.a is corrected as it's created in the source root, not the Lib/ subdir.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS='-O3 -fPIC -Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration' && \
    mkdir -p /usr/local/metis/include /usr/local/metis/lib && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/metis/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/metis/include/ && \
    cd /build && \
    # 2. Build Hypre 2.28.0
    # This is a dependency for MFEM. We configure with big-int support and without Fortran.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local/hypre --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd /build && \
    # 3. Build MFEM 4.7
    # This is the core finite element library dependency for Laghos.
    # We build the parallel (MPI) version, pointing to the METIS and Hypre installations.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/refs/tags/v4.7.tar.gz -O mfem-4.7.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf mfem-4.7.tar.gz && \
    cd mfem-4.7 && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local/hypre METIS_DIR=/usr/local/metis CXX=mpicxx && \
    cd /build && \
    # 4. Build Laghos
    # The final application build. It links against the previously built MFEM library.
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/build/mfem-4.7 && \
    # 5. Install the executable
    # Copy the final binary to a system-wide location on the PATH.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # 6. Prepare the runtime directory and copy data files
    mkdir -p /app && \
    cp data/* /app/ && \
    # 7. Cleanup build artifacts
    # Remove the entire build directory to reduce the final image size.
    cd / && rm -rf /build

# Set the default working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Base image for the build
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments
# This prevents issues with shared memory mechanisms (vader) and high-speed interconnects (openib)
# not typically available in standard container runtimes.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Install build dependencies, MPI, and required tools
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git, wget)
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \    
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create a build directory and compile all dependencies and the application from source
# This is done in a single RUN layer to optimize image size by allowing for cleanup of build artifacts.
RUN mkdir -p /build && cd /build && \
    # 1. Build METIS 4.0.3
    # This is a dependency for MFEM. We download, build, and manually install it.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS='-O3 -fPIC -Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration' && \
    mkdir -p /usr/local/metis/include /usr/local/metis/lib && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/metis/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/metis/include/ && \
    cd /build && \
    # 2. Build Hypre 2.28.0
    # This is a dependency for MFEM. We configure with big-int support and without Fortran.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local/hypre --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd /build && \
    # 3. Build MFEM 4.7
    # This is the core finite element library dependency for Laghos.
    # We build the parallel (MPI) version, pointing to the METIS and Hypre installations.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/refs/tags/v4.7.tar.gz -O mfem-4.7.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf mfem-4.7.tar.gz && \
    cd mfem-4.7 && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local/hypre METIS_DIR=/usr/local/metis CXX=mpicxx && \
    cd /build && \
    # 4. Build Laghos
    # The final application build. It links against the previously built MFEM library.
    # The LIBS variable is added to explicitly provide the linker with the METIS library path.
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/build/mfem-4.7 LIBS="-L/usr/local/metis/lib" && \
    # 5. Install the executable
    # Copy the final binary to a system-wide location on the PATH.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # 6. Prepare the runtime directory and copy data files
    mkdir -p /app && \
    cp data/* /app/ && \
    # 7. Cleanup build artifacts
    # Remove the entire build directory to reduce the final image size.
    cd / && rm -rf /build

# Set the default working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Base image for the build
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments
# This prevents issues with shared memory mechanisms (vader) and high-speed interconnects (openib)
# not typically available in standard container runtimes.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Install build dependencies, MPI, and required tools
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git, wget)
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \    
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create a build directory and compile all dependencies and the application from source
# This is done in a single RUN layer to optimize image size by allowing for cleanup of build artifacts.
RUN mkdir -p /build && cd /build && \
    # 1. Build METIS 4.0.3
    # This is a dependency for MFEM. We download, build, and manually install it.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS='-O3 -fPIC -Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration' && \
    mkdir -p /usr/local/metis/include /usr/local/metis/lib && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/metis/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/metis/include/ && \
    cd /build && \
    # 2. Build Hypre 2.28.0
    # This is a dependency for MFEM. We configure with big-int support and without Fortran.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local/hypre --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd /build && \
    # 3. Build MFEM 4.7
    # This is the core finite element library dependency for Laghos.
    # We build the parallel (MPI) version, pointing to the METIS and Hypre installations.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/refs/tags/v4.7.tar.gz -O mfem-4.7.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf mfem-4.7.tar.gz && \
    cd mfem-4.7 && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local/hypre METIS_DIR=/usr/local/metis CXX=mpicxx && \
    cd /build && \
    # 4. Build Laghos
    # The final application build. It links against the previously built MFEM library.
    # The problematic LIBS override is removed to allow the makefile to inherit all necessary linker
    # flags from the MFEM build, resolving undefined reference errors.
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/build/mfem-4.7 && \
    # 5. Install the executable
    # Copy the final binary to a system-wide location on the PATH.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # 6. Prepare the runtime directory and copy data files
    mkdir -p /app && \
    cp data/* /app/ && \
    # 7. Cleanup build artifacts
    # Remove the entire build directory to reduce the final image size.
    cd / && rm -rf /build

# Set the default working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Base image for the build
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments
# This prevents issues with shared memory mechanisms (vader) and high-speed interconnects (openib)
# not typically available in standard container runtimes.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Install build dependencies, MPI, and required tools
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git, wget)
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \    
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create a build directory and compile all dependencies and the application from source
# This is done in a single RUN layer to optimize image size by allowing for cleanup of build artifacts.
RUN mkdir -p /build && cd /build && \
    # 1. Build METIS 4.0.3
    # This is a dependency for MFEM. We download, build, and manually install it.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS='-O3 -fPIC -Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration' && \
    mkdir -p /usr/local/metis/include /usr/local/metis/lib && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/metis/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/metis/include/ && \
    cd /build && \
    # 2. Build Hypre 2.28.0
    # This is a dependency for MFEM. We configure with big-int support and without Fortran.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local/hypre --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd /build && \
    # 3. Build MFEM 4.7
    # This is the core finite element library dependency for Laghos.
    # The METIS_LIBS variable is explicitly set to ensure the correct linker path (-L/usr/local/metis/lib)
    # is embedded in MFEM's configuration for downstream use by Laghos.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/refs/tags/v4.7.tar.gz -O mfem-4.7.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf mfem-4.7.tar.gz && \
    cd mfem-4.7 && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local/hypre METIS_DIR=/usr/local/metis METIS_LIBS='-L/usr/local/metis/lib -lmetis' CXX=mpicxx && \
    cd /build && \
    # 4. Build Laghos
    # The final application build. It links against the previously built MFEM library.
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/build/mfem-4.7 && \
    # 5. Install the executable
    # Copy the final binary to a system-wide location on the PATH.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # 6. Prepare the runtime directory and copy data files
    mkdir -p /app && \
    cp data/* /app/ && \
    # 7. Cleanup build artifacts
    # Remove the entire build directory to reduce the final image size.
    cd / && rm -rf /build

# Set the default working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Base image for the build
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments
# This prevents issues with shared memory mechanisms (vader) and high-speed interconnects (openib)
# not typically available in standard container runtimes.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Install build dependencies, MPI, and required tools
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git, wget)
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \    
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create a build directory and compile all dependencies and the application from source
# This is done in a single RUN layer to optimize image size by allowing for cleanup of build artifacts.
RUN mkdir -p /build && cd /build && \
    # 1. Build METIS 4.0.3
    # This is a dependency for MFEM. We download, build, and manually install it.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS='-O3 -fPIC -Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration' && \
    mkdir -p /usr/local/metis/include /usr/local/metis/lib && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/metis/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/metis/include/ && \
    cd /build && \
    # 2. Build Hypre 2.28.0
    # This is a dependency for MFEM. We configure with big-int support and without Fortran.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local/hypre --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd /build && \
    # 3. Build MFEM 4.7
    # This is the core finite element library dependency for Laghos.
    # METIS_INC and METIS_LIB are explicitly set to provide the precise header and library paths,
    # ensuring MFEM's generated config is correct for the downstream Laghos build.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/refs/tags/v4.7.tar.gz -O mfem-4.7.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf mfem-4.7.tar.gz && \
    cd mfem-4.7 && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local/hypre METIS_INC='-I/usr/local/metis/include' METIS_LIB='-L/usr/local/metis/lib -lmetis' CXX=mpicxx && \
    cd /build && \
    # 4. Build Laghos
    # The final application build. It links against the previously built MFEM library.
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/build/mfem-4.7 && \
    # 5. Install the executable
    # Copy the final binary to a system-wide location on the PATH.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # 6. Prepare the runtime directory and copy data files
    mkdir -p /app && \
    cp data/* /app/ && \
    # 7. Cleanup build artifacts
    # Remove the entire build directory to reduce the final image size.
    cd / && rm -rf /build

# Set the default working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app
